HEADSS for Adolescents (HEADSS) 
Keywords: 
Adolescents 
Background: 
This is an interview instrument for finding out about issues in adolescents' lives. It was
developed by Cohen and colleagues (Cohen et al., 1991) 
Developer(s): 
Eric Cohen, Richard G. MacKenzie, and Gary L. Yates 
Copyright: 
Publisher: Elsevier 
Assessment:
Home 
l   Who lives with the young person? Where? 
l   Do they have their own room? 
l   What are relationships like at home? 
l   What do parents and relatives do for a living? 
l   Ever institutionalized? Incarcerated? 
l   Recent moves? Running away? 
l   New people in home environment? 
Education and employment 
l   School/grade performance--any recent changes? Any dramatic past changes? 
l   Favorite subjects--worst subjects? (include grades) 
l   Any years repeated/classes failed

l   Suspension, termination, dropping out? 
l   Future education/employment plans? 
l   Any current or past employment? 
l   Relations with teachers, employers--school, work attendance? 
Activities 
l   On own, with peers (what do you do for fun?, where? when?) 
l   With family? 
l   Sports--regular exercise? 
l   Church attendance, clubs, projects? 
l   Hobbies--other activities? 
l   Reading for fun--what? 
l   TV--how much weekly--favorite shows? 
l   Favorite music? 
l   Does young person have car, use seat belts? 
l   History of arrests--acting out--crime? 
Drugs 
l   Use by peers? Use by young person? (include tobacco, alcohol) 
l   Use by family members? (include tobacco, alcohol) 
l   Amounts, frequency, patterns of use/abuse, and car use while intoxicated? 
l   Source--how paid for? 
Sexuality 
l   Orientation? 
l   Degree and types of sexual experience and acts? 
l   Number of partners? 
l   Masturbation? (normalize) 
l   History of pregnancy/abortion? 
l   Sexually transmitted diseases--knowledge and prevention? Contraception?
Frequency of use? 
l   Comfort with sexual activity, enjoyment/pleasure obtained? History of
sexual/physical abuse? 
Suicide/Depression 
l   Sleep disorders (usually induction problems, also early/frequent waking or greatly
increased sleep and complaints of increasing fatigue)

l   Appetite/eating behavior changes 
l   Feelings of 'boredom' 
l   Emotional outbursts and highly impulsive behavior 
l   History of withdrawal/isolation 
l   Hopeless/helpless feelings 
l   History of past suicide attempts, depression, psychological counseling 
l   History of suicide attempts in family or peers 
l   History of recurrent serious 'accidents' 
l   Psychosomatic symptomology 
l   Suicidal ideation (including significant current and past losses) 
l   Decreased affect on interview, avoidance of eye contact--depression posturing 
l   Preoccupation with death (clothing, media, music, art). 
References: 
l   Goldenring, J, Cohen, E (1988) Getting into adolescents heads. Contemporary
Pediatrics, July: 75-80. 
l   Cohen, E, MacKenzie, R.G., Yates, G.L. (1991). HEADSS, a psychosocial risk
assessment instrument: Implications for designing effective intervention programs
for runaway youth. Journal of Adolescent Health 12 (7): 539-544.
